talks.title: Hacking Security Leadership
talks.teaser: Explores the skills, business alignment, and strategic mindset required to transition into cybersecurity leadership and executive roles.
talks.summary:
In this executive briefing from the DEF CON Safe Mode Career Hacking Village, the speaker addresses how technical security practitioners can master corporate communication and evolve into effective security leaders. Opening at 00:04, the presentation examines the common pitfall of framing security issues purely in technical terms rather than alignment with business objectives.

At 12:00 and 24:00, the speaker shares practical lessons on managing corporate risk, explaining that successful CISOs must abandon obstructionist risk avoidance in favor of risk management frameworks that enable business operations securely.

Concluding at 36:00 and 48:02, the presenter emphasizes emotional courage and transparency, advising emerging executives to deliver candid, data-driven risk assessments and provide actionable remediation paths rather than resorting to fear, uncertainty, and doubt. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Pwning Your Resume
talks.teaser: Actionable advice from a veteran recruiter on optimizing technical resumes, highlighting impact, and beating applicant tracking systems.
talks.summary:
Technical recruiter Kris Rides joins host Kathleen in the Career Hacking Village to share actionable guidance on optimizing cybersecurity resumes for competitive industry hiring pipelines [00:04, 00:12]. Rides cautions candidates against hiring generalist resume writers who lack familiarity with specialized technical roles, advising practitioners to take personal ownership of translating their hands-on skills [10:55].

The session identifies frequent resume shortcomings, including vague employment date ranges that raise red flags for recruiters [21:31] and the risk of oversharing sensitive proprietary details or non-disclosure agreement (NDA) project data [31:54]. Rides provides strategic recommendations for highlighting capture-the-flag (CTF) achievements, home lab environments, and industry certifications, concluding with tactical advice on building genuine professional relationships by connecting directly with hiring managers and conference speakers [42:34].

talks.title: Cons & Careers
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how attending hacker conventions, participating in village activities, and community networking accelerate career growth.
talks.summary:
In this career development session from the DEF CON Safe Mode Career Hacking Village, the speaker explores how participating in hacker conferences accelerates professional growth and technical mastery. Opening at 00:04, the presentation highlights conferences as essential hubs for skill development, networking, and community contribution.

At 12:00 and 24:00, the speaker provides strategies for navigating massive conferences, advising attendees to immerse themselves in specialized villages and hands-on labs where organic mentorship and authentic peer connections occur.

Addressing public speaking past 36:00 and 48:01, the presenter demystifies the CFP process, encouraging technical practitioners to share their research, embrace constructive vulnerability, and leverage conference presentations to challenge held assumptions and expand their professional horizons. talks.title: National Service Panel
talks.teaser: A panel exploring civilian and military public service pathways in federal cybersecurity, intelligence, and national defense.
talks.summary:
Joe Billingsley, founder of the Military Cyber Professionals Association (MCPA), convenes a panel of federal defense leaders and agency representatives to explore technology careers across United States national service in the Career Hacking Village [00:19, 00:33].

The panelists examine the diverse roles available across civilian and defense agencies, highlighting the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) mandate as the nation's risk advisor protecting critical infrastructure, federal networks, and election systems [03:41, 04:04]. Representatives from the National Security Agency (NSA) and military cyber branches outline operational opportunities, educational pipelines through the National Cryptologic School [07:48], and specialized direct commissioning programs that enable experienced technologists to enter military cyber services [16:58, 25:28], emphasizing public-private collaboration in national defense.

talks.title: The Individual Contributor to Tech Executive
talks.teaser: Navigating the career inflection point between remaining a hands-on individual contributor and stepping into executive leadership.
talks.summary:
In this insightful guide from the DEF CON Safe Mode Career Hacking Village, the speaker charts the professional roadmap for transitioning from an individual contributor (IC) to a senior technology executive. Opening at 00:20, the presentation explores the critical decision points that technical professionals encounter when evaluating leadership versus technical fellow career tracks.

At 07:01, the speaker discusses recognizing when one's interests shift from hands-on implementation toward strategic leadership, mentoring, and organizational design.

At 14:00 and 21:00, the talk contrasts the immediate satisfaction of technical debugging with the deliberate patience required for executive governance, cross-functional diplomacy, and policy formulation, offering practical guidance on developing executive presence and business acumen. talks.title: Entrepreneurial Adventures
talks.teaser: Bryson Bort shares hard-won lessons, pitfalls, and mindset strategies from founding and scaling cybersecurity startups.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity founder and SCYTHE CEO Bryson Bort delivers an honest, practical guide to navigating technology entrepreneurship and building security startups in the Career Hacking Village [00:04]. Bort details the journey from technical practitioner to chief executive, outlining the psychological and operational shifts required to found a commercial security venture [08:59].

The presentation breaks down the core phases of startup growth, examining ideation, navigating angel and seed investment rounds, and understanding the nuances of equity dilution and board governance [16:54, 25:00]. Bort shares operational realities of scaling an engineering business, discussing strategies for hiring collaborative technical teams, establishing baseline workplace culture, and evolving organizational policies as companies expand from early-stage prototypes into mature enterprises [33:23, 41:37].
